name: 2026-11-24-benchmarks

taskSet.name: repository benchmark: the five smallest eligible single-file commits of the last 400 (their hashes are in report.json)

regenerate.command: pnpm run transpile-client && ONYX_BENCH_OLLAMA=<Ollama root> ONYX_BENCH_LMSTUDIO=<LM Studio root> node test/onyx/run-benchmarks.mts --speculative --json-out docs/benchmarks/2026-11-24/report.json

notes: The raw reports behind the charts in the README. report.json: both runtimes, every section, at commit aa32e8f19ef with a clean tree; its speculative section is the older method (one prompt, best of three) and is superseded by speculative.json, which make-charts reads after it. speculative.json: the speculative comparison alone, code and prose apart, medians of three, the draft proven attached from LM Studio's REST list, at commit 373fc58cd97 with a clean tree. Ollama 0.33.0 and LM Studio 0.4.23 on private loopback ports, one model resident at a time; LM Studio's version is the one it records (report.json has null for it: the reader was fixed after that run). LM Studio's 7B and 1.5B GGUF files are byte-identical to Ollama's weight layers (the same digests), so the two runtimes are compared on the same weights. The two seeds are those of the pure-logic fuzz sections; no seed is sent with a model request. Each model ran at its runtime's own allocation: Ollama 4,096 tokens, LM Studio 8,192 (docs/research/results/2026-11-21-context-allocation, 2026-11-22-lmstudio-context). Load average: report.json 4.04 at the start and 19.13 at the end; speculative.json 14.02 and 15.98, on 14 cores. The owner was working on the machine; throughput for the 7B model matched the idle figure of 2026-11-21 (49 tok/s), and the speculative medians matched two separate lab runs (docs/research/results/2026-11-24-speculative).
